page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. A printed ornament (& flourish) stands at the lower right below the last line. The left edge carries a strip of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: sule, hanc frequens meditare, hanc imbibe penitus & in Animam tuam transfunde. Vides in Te omni-um conjectos oculos, in Te omnium Bonorum spes sitas, ex Te om-nium vitas pendere, quas jamdiu multi tædio projecissent, nisi ut essent quas tibi impenderent. Mag-num onus incumbit, magna urget procella, magna expectatio. Major omnium quam quæ unquam superiùs, Virtutum necessitas: An sit Regnum amplius in Britannia futurum, an Religio, an Homi-nes, an Deus, ex tuâ Virtute, -Tuâ Fortunâ dependet,Immo, sola potius ex Deo Fortuna: cujus opem quo magis hîc necessariam agnoscis, præsentaneam requiris, eò magis ma-gisque (quod jam facis) omni pie-tatis officio promereris; & illa quæ in Te large sparsit Bonitatis,Pru-dentiæ, Temperantiæ, Justitiæ,

page.notes: Printed ornament "&" with flourish at the lower right, below the last line; not a catchword or signature, so not transcribed as text. No page number, running head, catchword or signature is printed. "dependet,Immo" is printed without a space and is copied as it stands. The first letter of the first line is an italic f-form read as long s ("sule"). Marks "-Tuâ" and "Fortuna:" are copied as printed. The word "banc" on the first line is read as "hanc" (the h is partly worn). The left edge shows the neighbouring page and is not part of this page.
